column1: A one-time password (recover-admin, or user create --one-time-password) stayed valid for login until the user changed it, so an admin credential printed on a terminal, or relayed out of band and never used, was a live secret indefinitely (the 15-minute restricted SESSION did not bound the PASSWORD). Now each is stored with an expiry (users.one_time_password_expires_at, written in the same insert/transaction as the hash; recover-admin default 24h via security.recovery_one_time_password_ttl, admin-created default 72h via security.one_time_password_ttl, no value means never) and VerifyPasswordCredentials refuses an expired one after the bcrypt comparison with the same error as a wrong password (no oracle: status and body byte-identical over HTTP, latency matched), counts it toward the account lockout and audits auth.one_time_password_expired server-side; SetPasswordHash clears the expiry so a chosen password never expires this way. Upgrade: pre-existing password_reset_required accounts get upgrade time + 24h once, in the migration that adds the column (SQLite and Postgres). Proving tests: TestOneTimePassword_ExpiredIsRefusedLikeAWrongPassword, TestOneTimePassword_ExpiredAttemptsCountTowardLockout, TestLogin_ExpiredOneTimePassword_SameResponseAsWrongPassword (server/http), TestPerformRecoverAdmin_OneTimePasswordExpiry_RefusedAtLoginAfterExpiry, TestMigrateDatabase_OneTimePasswordExpiry_UpgradeBackfill; e2e journey scripts/e2e/journeys/journey21_otp_expiry_test.go.
